title: Finite reduction of the Poincare pairing
statement:
Use the smooth Poincare setting, with
the admissible structure morphism and normalized smooth orientation.
Let $n\geq m\geq1$, put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and
$A_m=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$, and let $K_n$ be a
site-perfect constructible
$A_n$-complex. Put $K_m=K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m$.
The coefficient comparisons identify the reduction of the
derived Poincare pairing
for $K_n$ with the pairing for $K_m$. In particular, writing
$K_n^\vee$ for its coefficient dual,
the canonical isomorphisms make the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
R\Gamma_c(X,K_n)^\vee\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m
&\xrightarrow{\beta_{K_n}^{\sharp,-1}\otimes1}&
R\Gamma(X,K_n^\vee(d))[2d]\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\\
\downarrow\wr&&\downarrow\wr\\
R\Gamma_c(X,K_m)^\vee
&\xrightarrow{\beta_{K_m}^{\sharp,-1}}&
R\Gamma(X,K_m^\vee(d))[2d]
\end{array}
$$

commute. Here $\beta^{\sharp,-1}$ denotes the inverse of the
tensor–Hom adjoint of the pairing.

proof.text: Write $\operatorname{red}_T(-)=(-)\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m$ on $T=X,s$. In the conventions [def-pod-conventions], the input $K_n$ is a site-perfect bounded constructible finite-Tor complex. The reduction functor has target $D^b_{ctf}(T,A_m)$ as stated in [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity]. Moreover $K_m=\operatorname{red}_XK_n$ is site-perfect: on any cover giving the model of [def-weil-site-perfect-complex], tensor the bounded finite-projective model termwise with $A_m$. This computes the derived tensor: finite-projective terms are flat since their tensor functors are retracts of finite sums of the identity, and the bounded-above flat-complex lemma [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes the model K-flat. Each term remains a direct summand of a finite free module, because tensoring the two splitting maps preserves their composite identity. The local condition of [def-weil-site-perfect-complex] at a finite stage is word for word the condition defining perfectness over $\Lambda_X$ in [def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x] (a pro-etale cover on which the complex is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective modules), and $K_n,K_m$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}$; so $K_n$ and $K_m$ are perfect over $A_{n,X}$ and $A_{m,X}$ respectively, which is the hypothesis of the duality and identification theorems used in steps 2 and 6. Thus the pairing and duality assertions for site-perfect inputs apply at both stages.

source.place: Opening hypotheses; site-perfectness needed for the first and last sentences of the proof

proof.text: Use the coefficient dual and its evaluation of [def-pod-coefficient-dual-on-x]. The site-perfect internal-Hom and evaluation clauses of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] give $\operatorname{red}_X(K_n^\vee)\cong K_m^\vee$, carrying the reduction of $\operatorname{ev}_{K_n}$ to $\operatorname{ev}_{K_m}$. By [thm-sf-dual-perfect], the dual remains perfect and the orientation-induced identification $\mathbb D_XK\cong K^\vee(d)[2d]$ is compatible with reduction, shifts and evaluation. Put $L_i=K_i^\vee(d)[2d]$ for $i=n,m$; its indicated comparison identifies $\operatorname{red}_XL_n$ with $L_m$. The smooth trace is the orientation followed by the exceptional counit, precisely the composite in [def-pur-smooth-trace]. The orientation and trace comparison squares commute by [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity], applied to $a_X$ and the coefficient unit.

source.place: First paragraph, internal Hom, evaluation, normalized trace and smooth orientation

proof.text:
Put $C_i=R\Gamma_c(X,K_i)$ and $D_i=R\Gamma(X,L_i)$. Here $L_i$ is bounded constructible finite-Tor by step 2 and the twist and shift conventions. Applying [thm-pod-point-perfectness] to $L_i$ shows that $D_i$ is a perfect point complex, hence lies in $D^b_{ctf}(s,A_i)$ as required by the projection transformation defining the cup product. The compact-support clause of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] gives the canonical isomorphism $c:\operatorname{red}_sC_n\xrightarrow{\sim}C_m$. Keep the ordinary comparison $r:\operatorname{red}_sD_n\to D_m$ as a morphism at this point: under $La_{X,m}^*\dashv Ra_{X*,m}$ of [fix-prop-adjunctions], it is the adjoint of
$$La_{X,m}^*\operatorname{red}_sRa_{X*,n}L_n\cong\operatorname{red}_XLa_{X,n}^*Ra_{X*,n}L_n\xrightarrow{\operatorname{red}_X(\varepsilon_n)}\operatorname{red}_XL_n\cong L_m.$$
Here the first comparison is the pullback comparison of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. The mixed-support cup product of [def-pod-mixed-support-cup-product] is the projection transformation followed by this ordinary counit. The tensor and compact-support comparisons preserve the projection transformation because they preserve its defining adjunction maps, units and counits, as stated in [lem-fix-operation-reduction]; the counit square is exactly the defining transpose equation for $r$. Composing these two squares gives
$$c_{K_n\otimes L_n}\circ\operatorname{red}_s(\smile_{c,n})=\smile_{c,m}\circ(c\otimes r),$$
with the canonical tensor and $L_i$ comparisons understood. This uses no inverse of $r$.

source.place: Second paragraph, composing the cup-product squares using only the canonical ordinary-global-section comparison

proof.text:
The pairing in [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing] is exactly cup product, followed by compactly supported evaluation, followed by the normalized trace. Compose the cup-product identity from step 3 with the evaluation and trace squares of step 2. Under the canonical tensor-unit identification $\operatorname{red}_sA_n\cong A_m$, this gives the equality of morphisms $\operatorname{red}_sC_n\otimes^L_{A_m}\operatorname{red}_sD_n\to A_m$,
$$\operatorname{red}_s(\beta_{K_n})=\beta_{K_m}\circ(c\otimes r).$$
It proves the asserted coefficient compatibility of the pairing itself.

source.place: Second paragraph, the commuting square for the pairing

proof.text:
By [thm-pod-point-perfectness], $C_n$ and $C_m$ are perfect point complexes; the theorem applies to our separated finite-type $X_0$ without any properness hypothesis. The point case of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] therefore gives the evaluation-compatible isomorphism $h:\operatorname{red}_s(C_n^\vee)\xrightarrow{\sim}(\operatorname{red}_sC_n)^\vee$. Define
$$\ell=(c^{-1})^\vee\circ h:\operatorname{red}_s(C_n^\vee)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_m^\vee.$$
This is the left vertical map in the statement. Its direction is forced by contravariance: dualize $c^{-1}:C_m\to\operatorname{red}_sC_n$, not $c$. It satisfies
$$\operatorname{ev}_{C_m}\circ(c\otimes\ell)=\operatorname{red}_s(\operatorname{ev}_{C_n})$$
under the tensor comparisons, by evaluation compatibility of $h$ and naturality of evaluation for the inverse isomorphisms $c,c^{-1}$.

source.place: Second paragraph, perfectness at the point and the left vertical isomorphism

proof.text:
Let $b_i^\sharp:D_i\xrightarrow{\sim}C_i^\vee$ be the tensor–Hom adjoint of $\beta_{K_i}$. These are isomorphisms by [thm-pod-identification-of-the-comparison] at $A_n$ and $A_m$, since step 1 verified site-perfectness at both stages. The uncurrying and evaluation formulas of [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] identify the uncurrying of $b_m^\sharp\circ r$ with $\beta_{K_m}\circ(1_{C_m}\otimes r)$. Precompose with $c\otimes1$ and use step 4; the result is $\operatorname{red}_s(\beta_{K_n})$. For the other morphism, the evaluation formula gives the precomposed uncurrying explicitly as
$$\operatorname{ev}_{C_m}\circ(c\otimes\ell)\circ(1\otimes\operatorname{red}_s(b_n^\sharp))
=\operatorname{red}_s(\operatorname{ev}_{C_n})\circ(1\otimes\operatorname{red}_s(b_n^\sharp))
=\operatorname{red}_s(\beta_{K_n}).$$
The first equality is step 5; the second is the adjoint evaluation identity and the tensor/evaluation compatibility of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Cancel the isomorphism $c\otimes1$ and use injectivity of the adjunction bijection (equivalently the inverse curry/uncurry identities of [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws]). Thus
$$b_m^\sharp\circ r=\ell\circ\operatorname{red}_s(b_n^\sharp).$$
Multiplying by the two horizontal inverses yields
$$r\circ\operatorname{red}_s((b_n^\sharp)^{-1})=(b_m^\sharp)^{-1}\circ\ell.$$
In particular $r=(b_m^\sharp)^{-1}\circ\ell\circ\operatorname{red}_s(b_n^\sharp)$ is an isomorphism: all three factors are isomorphisms. The last equality is exactly the displayed square, with its canonical right vertical comparison. Every tensor product used here is derived; the argument uses perfectness of $C_n$, not flatness of $A_m$ as an $A_n$-module.

source.place: Second paragraph, taking adjoints, proving the right comparison invertible and taking horizontal inverses

proof_origin.place: Complete proof; six explicit steps realizing the two paragraphs

split_report.summary: Expanded the imported paragraph into six argument steps, constructed the ordinary comparison without assuming invertibility, spelled out the cup/evaluation/trace identity, the contravariant dual of compact-support comparison and the adjunction calculation giving the inverse square. Reused existing nodes including the monoidal-closed uncurrying leaf. Kept the statement, current blueprint route and all import metadata unchanged; no new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Current main-20261015 thm-pod-finite-reduction.proof.md: first paragraph realized by steps 1-2; cup and pairing comparisons in second paragraph by steps 3-4; point perfectness and inverse-adjoint square by steps 5-6. This is an auxiliary node, not the statement of sk-thm-sf-package, so the unit realized fields are not changed.

tool_uses.why: The general ringed-site fact that bounded-above flat complexes are K-flat justifies computing reduction on a strict perfect local model. It is used as a homological-algebra tool, without changing the unit route.

I read the delivery in full: the item thm-pod-finite-reduction, its six steps, every cited node's statement, and the current blueprint statement and proof (main-20261015). There are no new nodes. The statement matches main-20261015 word for word and is not weakened. The coefficient categories are the finite pro-etale categories D^b_ctf with base change -⊗^L_{A_n}A_m, the same functor that thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity uses. Every cited unit is on the route of sk-thm-sf-package. There is no cycle, and proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses. I accept the tool use lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site: it is a generic K-flatness fact, and I read Stacks 06YQ, sites-cohomology.tex line 3120. Step checks. Step 1: a site-perfect local model, tensored termwise, computes the derived reduction. Step 2: lem-fix-operation-reduction is used only within its finite-stage, site-perfect internal-Hom clause, and thm-sf-dual-perfect and thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity give the orientation and trace squares. Step 3: thm-pod-point-perfectness puts D_i in D^b_ctf(s); r is built as the adjunction mate under fix-prop-adjunctions, and its inverse is never used. Step 4: elementary composition of the earlier squares. Step 5: ℓ=(c^{-1})^∨∘h, and I re-derived its evaluation identity from naturality of evaluation. Step 6: I re-derived b_m^♯ r = ℓ red(b_n^♯) from the uncurry laws (Mathlib lines 175, 180 and 194) and from thm-pod-identification-of-the-comparison at both stages; this proves r invertible and gives the displayed square. Edge cases checked: n=m, K=0, X=Spec k with d=0, n=2 and m=1 (A_1 not flat over A_2), and X not proper. The fault: steps 2 and 6 apply theorems that require K to be perfect over Λ_X (def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x), but the item only shows site-perfectness and never connects the two notions. They state the same local condition, so in the fixed item JSON I added one sentence to step 1 and cited def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x in step 1's uses and in proof_deps; nothing else changed. A source error in another node is reported, not fixed: lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site gives Stacks tag 06YS in source.place, but the tag table shows the correct tag is 06YQ (06YS is lemma-K-flat-resolution).; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
